Rule and exact checklists:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.",
  "Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.",
  "Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.",
  "Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty."
]

Claimed finding status: deviation

Claimed target and element mapping:
{"level":"preferred","mappings":[{"element":"Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1,2]},{"element":"Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.","status":"already_met","quote":"Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits"}]}

Finding rationale:
Section 5(a) imposes an unconditional minimum monthly fee for both Hosting Services and Support Services regardless of Client's actual usage, and Section 6 expressly strips Client of any right to documentation for, or to contest, those minimum monthly fees. That is a take-or-pay floor that recurs in each automatically renewing one-year term (Section 13). It fails the fallback on material terms: there is no right to reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice (Client's only exit is whole-agreement termination under Section 14, effective as late as the last day of the month following notice) and no true-up mechanic for underused volumes. The proposal takes the preferred position with two surgical deletions: the fee floor in Section 5(a) is removed so fees are payable only for requested services, and the now-dangling "minimum monthly fees" carve-outs in Section 6 are conformed. Section 3(i) (ordering a credit report on each borrower submitted through the Interface) is a usage-triggered sourcing term, not a minimum volume commitment, and the storage/bandwidth figures in Section 3 are service specifications rather than commitments on Client, so neither is flagged.

Original cited paragraphs:
p0045: a. Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services). For any other services agreed to between the parties, Client will pay TrueLink fees which will be determined by the parties and will vary depending on the services utilized. TrueLink will provide Client with an invoice for the requested Hosting Services and Support Services and any other agreed-upon services on a monthly basis. Invoices will be paid within 15 days of receipt.
p0047: 6. DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES. Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4), provided that Client timely pays all contested amounts. TrueLink agrees that the costs for any Hosting Services will not increase for a period of one year from the date of this Agreement and that rates charged for Hosting Services will not exceed that charged by TrueLink to any other party.

TrueLink: This Agreement is entered into on February 26, 1999, (the "Effective Date") by and between Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. Hosting Services: 3. HOSTING SERVICES. TrueLink will provide the following services to Client (the "Hosting Services"):

Rendered operative language:
a. Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, and Client will have no minimum purchase or volume commitment. For any other services agreed to between the parties, Client will pay TrueLink fees which will be determined by the parties and will vary depending on the services utilized. TrueLink will provide Client with an invoice for the requested Hosting Services and Support Services and any other agreed-upon services on a monthly basis. Invoices will be paid within 15 days of receipt.
6. DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES. Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged and will be entitled to contest any charge, provided that Client timely pays all contested amounts. TrueLink agrees that the costs for any Hosting Services will not increase for a period of one year from the date of this Agreement and that rates charged for Hosting Services will not exceed that charged by TrueLink to any other party.

Margin comment:
[Playbook] We removed the minimum monthly fees for Hosting and Support Services so that Client pays only for the services it requests, consistent with our no-minimum-commitment position, and conformed Section 6 so it no longer references the deleted minimums. If a floor is essential, we could accept one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice and trued up rather than penalised.

elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: no shortfall can arise because no minimum volume or fee floor remains, and no penalty, shortfall charge, or contingent payment formula is retained in Section 5(a) or Section 6.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.

elements.evidence: Limb (iv): "arising out of TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Revised 12(a) now reads only: "(i) any claim arising out of or relating to Client Content ... and (ii) any breach by Client of any applicable state or federal law, rule or regulation"; the breach-of-Agreement, System/Credit Repository default and product-injury limbs and the Web Site hook are removed.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Inserted limb (i) covers third-party claims that the Interface, related software, Hosting Services or Support Services infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the inserted paragraph delivers all four indemnity triggers (IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), an express defend duty extending to Client's affiliates, and the full notice / control-of-defence / reasonable-cooperation procedure; the revised 12(a) confines Client's indemnity to Client Content and Client's own breach of law.

The data-breach limb is drafted with a catch-all ("or any other data of Client, its affiliates or their respective customers that is provided to, transmitted through or processed by TrueLink"), so the artificially narrow § 1(d) Credit Data definition (31-day-old, archived, non-combined data) does not undercut the trigger.
Fallback is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace ladder, no refund backstop, no 3x annual fees super-cap), but position-completeness is satisfied at the preferred level, which is the claimed target.

Minimality holds: the insertion is a single concise paragraph tracking only the checklist elements, the deletions in 12(a) are exactly those required to narrow Customer's indemnity to content and breach of law, the favourable existing 12(b) TrueLink indemnity and the § 12 cap survive untouched, and no survival tail, expense allocation, extra damages categories or boilerplate were added.

Intent is preserved: no defined term is orphaned (Interface, Hosting Services, Support Services, Client Content and Credit Data all remain defined), no cross-reference dangles, and the retained 12(b) breach-of-Agreement indemnity is additive rather than contradictory to the new paragraph.

Optional drafting note (not a defect against the checklist): TrueLink is given control of settlement without a Client-consent proviso for settlements imposing liability or admissions on Client; if raised in negotiation, that could be tightened without affecting element coverage.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Document: EXHIBIT 10.4

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-3f975ee9","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 12(b) is TrueLink's only indemnity and is confined to claims arising out of TrueLink's breach of this Agreement or failure to perform; there is no duty to defend and no indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct (searches for \"infringe\", \"indemnif\" and \"hold harmless\" confirm no IP indemnity anywhere, including §§ 2, 8 and 9). Section 12(a) meanwhile imposes a very broad Client indemnity covering breach of the Agreement, System/Credit Repository defaults, Web Site claims and product/service injury. That fails the fallback (no Vendor IP indemnity at all) and is close to walk-away, so we target preferred. Op 2 adds the Vendor defend-and-indemnify obligation with notice, control of defence and cooperation; per the verifier, its data-breach limb now reaches Client Content, Credit Data and any other data of Client, its affiliates or their customers provided to, transmitted through or processed by TrueLink, so the narrow § 1(d) Credit Data definition (31-day-old, archived, non-combined data) no longer caps the trigger. Op 1 limits our indemnity to Client Content and our own breach of law, deleting the broad \"the Web Site or\" hook. \"Interface\", \"Hosting Services\", \"Support Services\", \"Client Content\" and \"Credit Data\" are all defined, and the § 12 cap (Sections 3, 4, 7, 11) and existing 12(b) indemnity survive unchanged.","proposal":"Add TrueLink IP/misconduct indemnity (including all Client data) with standard procedure and narrow Client's indemnity","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-ip-2ef3ea98","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT","rationale":"Section 8(d) grants TrueLink a worldwide licence to distribute, disseminate, license, resell and exploit our borrower Credit Data — independent exploitation of Customer Data going far beyond processing to provide the Services, which is walk-away territory under this rule and is not cured by any ownership statement elsewhere. The Agreement also contains no ownership or assignment of work product created for us (the Support Services results are only treated as Client Proprietary Information under Section 10) and no statement that we retain rights in Client Content and Credit Data or that nothing is jointly owned. TrueLink's retention of its own platform IP in Section 2(d) is acceptable and is preserved. We therefore narrow the Credit Data licence to service delivery and add the short preferred ownership clause.","proposal":"Narrow TrueLink's Credit Data licence to service delivery and add a Client ownership/assignment clause with a licence back to embedded TrueLink IP.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-657fe724","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"The only liability limitation in the Agreement (p0077, inside the indemnity section) caps TrueLink alone at 12 months' hosting and support compensation, while Client's liability — including the very broad Section 12(a) indemnity — remains unlimited. That is walk-away territory under the rule (Customer uncapped while Vendor capped), and the sole carve-out covers only TrueLink's gross negligence and wilful misconduct, with nothing for indemnification or confidentiality (Section 10). We therefore target the fallback with the smallest edit: \"TRUELINK'S LIABILITY\" becomes \"EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY\" so the cap binds both parties, and the parenthetical carve-out is made mutual and extended to indemnification obligations and breach of confidentiality obligations. The existing Section 3, 4, 7 and 11 scope and the 12-month compensation basis are retained verbatim, so TrueLink gains no new cap protection for matters (e.g. warranties, service performance) where it is presently uncapped. Preferred items not pressed here: the USD 1,000,000 floor, \"paid or payable\", anchoring the window to the event giving rise to the claim, a mutual indirect/consequential exclusion, carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud and IP infringement, and the payment-obligations exclusion.","proposal":"Make the existing Section 3/4/7/11 12-month fee cap mutual and carve out indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-assign-0ba91216","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 15 is the only assignment provision in the Agreement. It bars assignment by either party without the other's prior written approval, with a mutual carve-out only for a \"financially responsible affiliate\". It fails the fallback because there is no successor right at all (no merger/acquisition/asset-sale carve-out, no successor-with-notice construct) and no reasonableness standard on consent; the retained no-consent affiliate exception also cannot coexist with a fallback under which every non-successor assignment requires consent. Rather than strip our own affiliate right to reach fallback, we move to the preferred position: Client-only affiliate and successor assignment without approval, TrueLink assignment only with our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a competitor. No change-of-control termination right exists today, so the added confirmation is a clarification only.","proposal":"Client-side affiliate/successor assignment right; TrueLink assignment only with Client's consent, never to a competitor; no termination on Client change of control.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-d3c226c3","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 2 LICENSE.","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Client, so it sits at the preferred position. The licence in Section 2(a) is expressly non-exclusive and Section 2(a) affirmatively confirms Client \"is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret\" for similar software and services. Section 3(i)'s requirement to order credit reports from TrueLink bites only where Client voluntarily requests an underwriting approval \"through a System using the Interface\", so it is a sourcing condition on voluntary interface use rather than exclusive dealing, given the express freedom to use alternatives. The only competition-related restriction referenced (the Non-Competition Agreement in Section 8(d)) operates as a limitation on TrueLink's use of Credit Data and therefore benefits Client. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-863d5593","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalties, stipulated sums or early-termination charge on Client, so it meets our preferred position (Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties). Section 14 (p0079) lets Client elect to terminate with services simply running to the last day of the following month and attaches no termination fee or accelerated minimum payment; the non-renewal mechanic in Section 13 (p0078) is likewise fee-free. Compensation in Section 5 (p0045) is ordinary monthly consideration for services actually requested — the \"$____ per month\" floors are recurring minimum service charges, not a sum payable on termination or on breach, and the disputes clause (p0047) does not convert them into stipulated damages. The spam covenant in Section 7 (p0049) is a bare prohibition with no per-message or fixed-sum penalty against Client. The only monetary cap in the document (p0077) runs in our favour by limiting TrueLink's liability. Nothing to redline; we would resist any later insertion of a termination fee above three months' fees.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-c28d3f0c","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 2 LICENSE.","rationale":"No non-compete or field-of-use covenant binds Client anywhere in the Agreement, so the rule sits at our preferred position. Section 2(a) (p0022/p0024) affirmatively confirms Client is not obligated to use the License and is free to acquire, develop or license competing software and services (subject only to TrueLink IP and confidentiality), which is a benefit to us. Section 8 (Client covenants) contains only compliance, non-representation, access-control, IP warranty and anti-spam undertakings (p0049, p0051-p0058) — none restricts our lines of business or products. Two points noted but not flagged: (i) the Section 2(a) licence scope is tied to Client's consumer finance receivables business, which is an ordinary limit on the licensed Interface rather than a covenant restricting our own business; and (ii) Section 8(d) (p0054) cross-refers to an undefined, unattached \"Non-Competition Agreement\", but there it operates only to limit TrueLink's rights in Credit Data, not to restrict Client — we should still review that side agreement separately for any covenant binding us.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-9718b410","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 14 (p0079) gives Client an unconditional, no-cause election to terminate the Agreement at any time — a convenience right even though the word \"convenience\" is not used — with service simply continuing until the last day of the month following the month of notice (roughly 30-60 days' run-off). That is at or better than the fallback notice window of 60-90 days, and no early-termination fee, penalty or other exit charge appears anywhere in the Agreement, so the three-months-of-fees fee cap is comfortably satisfied. On the Vendor side, TrueLink has no mid-term termination-for-convenience right: Section 13 (p0078) permits mid-term cutting-off of Sections 2 and 3 only for Client breach/default events (for cause), and the only other exit is the mutual auto-renewal non-renewal notice given \"no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year,\" whose effect is expressly tied to the end of the then-current one-year term — that is natural-term non-renewal reviewed under RENEWAL, not a Vendor mid-term convenience right, so we do not flag it twice here. The initial term is one year, so the walk-away concern about no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term does not arise. Falling short of the preferred position only in that there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; this is immaterial because Section 5(a) (p0045) has TrueLink invoice monthly with invoices \"paid within 15 days of receipt,\" so fees are not prepaid. The clause therefore sits at (and in the Customer's favour, above) the fallback and we would not redline it.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-05add6c3","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5 COMPENSATION.","rationale":"No audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right binding Client exists anywhere in the Agreement. Searches for audit/inspect/records/verify/examine returned nothing, and full reads of § 2 (Licence and Hosting Services), § 5-6 (Compensation, Documentation and Disputes), § 8 (Client covenants), § 10 (Confidentiality) and §§ 12-30 confirm the only verification mechanic runs in our favour: § 6 gives Client the right to supporting documentation for charges and to contest them. The nearest TrueLink-side right, § 8(f) (\"TrueLink reserves the right at any time to implement technical mechanisms to prevent Client engaging in illegal or obscene activity or in 'spamming'\"), is a preventive technical measure on TrueLink's own hosted Interface, not an audit or inspection of Client, and confers no access to Client systems or records. Nothing therefore needs frequency, notice, business-hours, independent-auditor, cost-allocation or system-access limits, and no walk-away risk (unlimited/unannounced audits or remote access to Client systems) is present. We do not redline: inserting the preferred or fallback audit parameters would create a TrueLink audit right that does not exist today and would weaken our position. Note for the file only: if TrueLink later seeks usage verification, we would hold at once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, TrueLink's cost absent 5% underpayment, and no direct system access.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-f65d9023","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 26 (p0093) selects California law and Section 27 (p0094) fixes exclusive venue in the state or federal courts located within San Luis Obispo County, California, with consent to jurisdiction and waiver of forum objections. That sits squarely at the fallback position: an accepted governing law (California) with the corresponding California courts as the merits forum. There is no arbitration provision anywhere in the document (searches for arbitration and dispute resolution returned nothing), so the walk-away scenario of mandatory arbitration seated abroad or a foreign exclusive venue does not arise. Short of the preferred position, the law is California rather than New York and the venue is TrueLink's home county (San Luis Obispo) rather than New York County, and the venue clause contains no express carve-out for temporary injunctive relief elsewhere — these are noted rather than redlined because the clause meets every fallback element on its material terms. Per playbook, a clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-c4aca5cc","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2 LICENSE.","rationale":"The grant in § 2(a) runs to \"Client\" only (defined in the preamble as Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. alone), with no affiliate coverage and no path to add affiliates, and § 15 bars any transfer of rights without TrueLink's prior written approval save for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate — so there is no successor/M&A transfer right for the licence. Both fallback elements therefore fail on material terms. We target the fallback: affiliates covered on written notice and a Client-only licence transfer to an M&A successor, made as an added exception in § 15 so the retained consent mechanic is not contradicted. The licence is not revocable at TrueLink's discretion (§ 2(c) ties it to termination under Section 12), so this is a deviation rather than walk-away; the absence of perpetual/irrevocable and contractor coverage is noted but not pursued at the preferred level.","proposal":"Extend licence to Client affiliates on written notice and permit transfer of the licence to an M&A successor without approval.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-ead09424","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5 COMPENSATION.","rationale":"The only MFN mechanic in the Agreement runs in our favour: in § 6 TrueLink commits that Hosting Services rates will not exceed those charged to any other party (plus a one-year price freeze). We reviewed the compensation terms (§ 5, § 6), the licence grant (§ 2), and Client's covenants (§ 8), and searched for \"no less favorable\", most-favoured, right-to-match and comparable-terms language: there is no obligation on Client to extend TrueLink terms given to other hosts or partners, and no obligation to match third-party offers. This meets the preferred position (no Customer MFN obligation benefiting Vendor), so no redline is proposed; the Vendor-granted MFN should be preserved.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-c94a73c9","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 5 COMPENSATION.","rationale":"Section 5(a) imposes an unconditional minimum monthly fee for both Hosting Services and Support Services regardless of Client's actual usage, and Section 6 expressly strips Client of any right to documentation for, or to contest, those minimum monthly fees. That is a take-or-pay floor that recurs in each automatically renewing one-year term (Section 13). {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Support and Licence Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Client-side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4 — findings and recommended positions

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. Nineteen rules were assessed: **six require redlines** (three critical, one high, two medium, one low, including two clauses that are simply absent), and **thirteen sit at or above our preferred or fallback positions and are not being touched**.

The risk profile is heavily one-sided. Three points drive the negotiation:

- **Risk allocation is inverted.** TrueLink's only indemnity is for its own breach, with no duty to defend and no IP, data-breach or misconduct cover, while Client gives a very broad indemnity (§ 12(a)). The single liability cap protects TrueLink alone at 12 months' hosting and support compensation and leaves Client uncapped — walk-away territory under the LOL-CAP rule.
- **Our data is licensed away.** § 8(d) grants TrueLink a worldwide right to distribute, license, resell and exploit borrower Credit Data independently of service delivery, and the Agreement contains no ownership or assignment of work product and no data-return or transition mechanic on exit.
- **Basic vendor protections are missing.** There is no conformance or services warranty (only a Year 2000 warranty in § 9), no insurance obligation of any kind, and no successor/M&A transfer right for either the Agreement or the licence.

Commercially, the minimum monthly fee floor in § 5(a) is a take-or-pay commitment that § 6 expressly insulates from documentation and challenge. Positive terms worth preserving: Client's unconditional exit right (§ 14), the 30-day non-renewal window and one-year renewal terms (§ 13), TrueLink's rate MFN and first-year price freeze (§ 6), Client's express freedom to use alternative suppliers (§ 2(a)), the absence of any audit, non-compete, non-solicit or liquidated-damages obligation on Client, and California law with California venue (§§ 26–27) — accepted at fallback.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary / position |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY | § 12(b) covers only TrueLink's own breach: no duty to defend, no IP, breach-of-law, data-breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct indemnity, against a very broad Client indemnity in § 12(a). Add Vendor defend-and-indemnify (notice, control of defence, cooperation) covering Client Content, Credit Data and other Client data; narrow our indemnity to Client Content and our own breach of law. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | § 8(d) licenses TrueLink to distribute, resell and exploit borrower Credit Data beyond service delivery (walk-away); no ownership/assignment of work product. Narrow the licence to service delivery and add a Client ownership clause with licence back to embedded TrueLink IP. § 2(d) TrueLink platform IP preserved. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY | Cap protects TrueLink only (12 months' hosting/support compensation); Client, including under § 12(a), is uncapped — walk-away. Make the existing §§ 3/4/7/11 cap mutual ("EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY") and extend the carve-out mutually to indemnification and confidentiality (§ 10) alongside gross negligence and wilful misconduct. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY | § 15 requires consent with no successor/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard. Seek Client-side affiliate and successor assignment without approval; TrueLink assignment only with our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a competitor; confirm no termination on Client change of control. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE | No exclusivity on Client; § 2(a) licence is non-exclusive and expressly preserves our freedom to acquire or develop alternatives. § 3(i) is a sourcing condition on voluntary Interface use only. Preferred position; no redline. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY | No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination charge on Client (§§ 13, 14 exits are fee-free; § 5 fees are ordinary monthly consideration). Preferred position; resist any later termination fee above three months' fees. |
| High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE | No non-compete or field-of-use covenant binds Client. Noted: § 8(d) cross-refers to an unattached "Non-Competition Agreement" which there limits TrueLink only — review that side agreement separately. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY | § 14 gives Client an unconditional no-cause exit (run-off to month-end following notice), no exit fee; TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right. At or above fallback. No pro-rata refund language, but fees are not prepaid (§ 5(a), monthly invoicing, 15 days). |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION | No audit or inspection right binding Client anywhere; § 6 verification runs in our favour. We will not insert audit parameters, as doing so would create a right that does not exist. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY | § 26 California law; § 27 exclusive venue in San Luis Obispo County, California; no arbitration. Fallback position — accepted, not redlined. |
| Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE | Grant runs to Client only, with no affiliate coverage and no successor transfer right (§ 15). Extend the licence to Client affiliates on written notice and permit transfer to an M&A successor without approval, drafted as an exception in § 15. |
| Medium | MFN | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION | The only MFN runs in our favour (§ 6 rate MFN plus one-year price freeze); no MFN burdens Client. Preferred position — preserve as drafted. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments | Deviation | § 5 COMPENSATION | § 5(a) imposes unconditional minimum monthly fees regardless of usage, recurring each renewal term (§ 13), and § 6 removes any right to documentation or to contest them. No reduction right and no true-up. Delete the fee floor and conform the § 6 carve-outs. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT | Compliant | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | No non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant anywhere. Preferred position; no redline. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY | § 13: one-year renewal terms with a 30-day mutual non-renewal notice; no unilateral uplift (Exhibits A/B, § 6 freeze and MFN, § 16 written-amendment requirement). Meets fallback and most of preferred; absence of a 60-day renewal reminder noted only. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY | No data return, export, migration assistance or deletion obligation (§§ 13, 14 place migration burdens on Client; § 10 has no return-or-destroy). Insert preferred clause: up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, return within 30 days in machine-readable format, certified deletion thereafter; fallback of 90 days / 30-day export offered in comment. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | TrueLink's only warranty is the § 9 Year 2000 warranty; no conformance or services warranty and no remedy. Insert fallback warranty: 90-day software conformance to documentation, 30-day services warranty, repair/replace or refund. The § 12 disclaimer is prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," so no consequential edit is needed. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY | No insurance obligation anywhere, although TrueLink hosts our Web Site and transmits consumer credit data. Insert a new Section 31: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M where TrueLink processes Client data, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request; fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following are identified in the findings as walk-away (or, for indemnity, close to walk-away) territory. We should not sign without movement on each:

1. **One-way liability cap (§ 12).** TrueLink capped at 12 months' hosting and support compensation while Client's liability, including the broad § 12(a) indemnity, is unlimited. Minimum acceptable outcome: the existing cap made mutual, with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
2. **Independent exploitation of borrower Credit Data (§ 8(d)).** The worldwide right to distribute, license, resell and exploit our Credit Data must be narrowed to what is needed to deliver the Services.
3. **No data return on exit.** Client Content ownership without any return, export or deletion mechanic. A transition and data-return clause must be added.
4. **No insurance of any kind**, in a relationship where TrueLink hosts our site and transmits consumer credit data.
5. **No Vendor IP or data-breach indemnity and no duty to defend**, set against a very broad Client indemnity — close to walk-away and the reason we are pressing the preferred position rather than a fallback.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the six items requiring change: indemnity (§ 12), ownership and the Credit Data licence (§ 8(d)), the mutual liability cap (§ 12), assignment and licence transfer (§ 15 / § 2), minimum monthly fees (§ 5(a) and conforming § 6 edits), warranty, transition/data return and the new insurance section.
2. **Sequence the negotiation:** treat the mutual cap, the Vendor indemnity, the Credit Data licence, data return and insurance as the priority set; the licence-scope and assignment edits are drafted as narrow exceptions and should be presentable as clean-up.
3. **Commercial input needed** on the § 5(a) minimum monthly fee floors — confirm whether removal is achievable or whether we should instead seek a reduction right on 30 days' notice plus a true-up as the fallback.
4. **Obtain and review the "Non-Competition Agreement"** cross-referenced in § 8(d); it is undefined and unattached, and we need to confirm it contains no covenant binding Client.
5. **Preserve on our side** the § 14 exit right, § 13 renewal mechanics, the § 6 MFN and price freeze, § 2(a) freedom to use alternatives, the absence of any audit, non-solicit, non-compete or liquidated-damages obligation, and §§ 26–27 governing law and venue at fallback. We are not opening these.
6. **File notes for a future round:** no 60-day renewal reminder; no USD 1,000,000 cap floor, "paid or payable" formulation or mutual consequential-loss exclusion; no express pro-rata refund on convenience termination; and the audit parameters we would hold to if TrueLink later seeks usage verification."}
